passage: I took some soup over to the flat next door and found Yamini walking the room with her son Vaibhav on her hip. He was hot-cheeked and whimpering, and every time she tried to set him on the cot he clutched her kurta and cried. She did not scold him. She gave him sips of water, spoke to him in a low steady voice and rocked him. "If he stays unwell, I will ring the doctor," she told me quietly.

qa.q: What did Yamini give Vaibhav to drink?
qa.a: She gave him sips of water.

qa.q: Why do you think Vaibhav clutched Yamini's kurta whenever she tried to put him down?
qa.a: He feels ill and hurt and wants the comfort of being held. It is a need for closeness, not naughtiness.

qa.q: What would you advise Yamini if Vaibhav's fever keeps going or worries her?
qa.a: Keep comforting him, and call the doctor rather than waiting, as she already plans to do.

qa.q: How might the neighbour's visit look to Yamini after a long day of holding Vaibhav?
qa.a: Yamini is probably tired and glad of some company and food, though the neighbour only saw part of the day and cannot know how worried she really felt.

grounding: A feverish or hurt child wants to be held and will not be put down; comfort, water and a steady voice are right, and a doctor if it worries.

passage:
Mother's note, Tuesday.

Vandana, two, had a fever all day and wouldn't be put down. Every time I tried, she wailed.

So I held her, gave her small sips of water and sang quietly. Naveen took over when my arms ached.

By evening the fever was still there and she was very sleepy, so we called the doctor, who asked us to bring her in. We did not scold her clinginess.

qa.q: Who took over holding Vandana when the mother's arms ached?
Why did Vandana wail every time she was put down?
qa.a: Vandana felt ill and scared, and needed the comfort and safety of being held.

qa.q: Which choices did the parents make that were right?
qa.a: They held and comforted her, gave water and rest, spoke calmly, didn't scold her clinginess, and called the doctor when she stayed feverish and very sleepy.

qa.q: How might Naveen be feeling while taking his turn?
qa.a: Naveen is probably worried about Vandana and wanting to help and comfort her.

grounding: Shows a feverish toddler who won't be put down, comforted with holding and water, with the doctor called when signs are worrying.

passage:
In their village house, Chetan, two, had a hot forehead and whimpered whenever his father Deepak put him on the mat.

Deepak picked him up and walked slowly around the courtyard, humming. He gave Chetan sips of water and stayed close.

Grandmother said, "Don't spoil him."

"He's sick. He needs me," Deepak said.

When the fever kept going next morning, they went to the health centre.

qa.q: Where did Deepak walk with Chetan?
What was Chetan feeling when he whimpered on the mat?
qa.a: Chetan felt unwell and scared, wanting to be held.

qa.q: What did Deepak do that was right?
qa.a: He held and calmed Chetan, gave water, didn't treat clinginess as spoiling, and took him to the health centre when the fever kept going.

qa.q: How does Grandmother see Deepak holding Chetan?
qa.a: Grandmother sees it as spoiling, while Deepak sees it as comfort Chetan needs when sick.

grounding: Shows a sick toddler who wants to be held, comforted with holding and water, with a doctor visit when the fever keeps going.
